reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (same order IDs and amounts, same count). Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and acme's net balance is 42714. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme (42714) and birch (65068) are done, so the last customer to check is cobalt. Getting cobalt's net balance next.
All three net balances are in and the refunds matched Alpha's report, so I can start paying. Recording acme's payout of 42714 first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance is 65068 and the refunds matched Alpha's report, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net balance is 2634, which matches its orders (4653 + 33845) less its refunds (2289 + 33575). Recording cobalt's payout now.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. I checked each against the orders and refunds: acme 46215 - 3501 = 42714, birch 29562 + 35506 = 65068 with no refunds, and cobalt 38498 - 35864 = 2634. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so no hold was needed.
